changes.text: 张之洞的铁路议奏写于一场争执之中：朝中就修不修铁路、修在哪里有几种主张。《清史稿·张之洞传》记：「會海軍衙門奏請修京通鐵路，臺諫爭陳鐵路之害，請停辦」。海军衙门主张修京通铁路；台谏（负责进言、弹劾的言官）争陈铁路之害，请停办。传文接着记了另外两种主张：「翁同龢等請試修邊地，便用兵；徐會灃請改修德州濟寧路，利漕運」。翁同龢等主张试修边地，理由是便于用兵；徐会沣主张改修德州济宁路，理由是利于漕运。传文在这几种主张之后，才录下本文传主张之洞的议奏。至于台谏所说的害具体是哪几条、海军衙门的理由为何，传文都没有记。

Zhang Zhidong's railway memorial was written in the middle of a dispute: at court there were several positions on whether to build railways and where. His biography in the Draft History of the Qing records it this way (here and throughout, quotations from the Chinese are our own translations): "When the Naval Office petitioned to build the Beijing-Tongzhou railway, the censors pressed the harms of railways and asked that the project be halted." The Naval Office stood for building the Beijing-Tongzhou line. The censors, the court's officials charged with remonstrance and impeachment, pressed the harms and asked for a stop. The biography then records two further proposals. Weng Tonghe and others asked to try building in the frontier regions, for ease of moving troops. Xu Huifeng asked to build a Dezhou-Jining line instead, for the benefit of grain transport. Only after these positions does the biography record the memorial of Zhang Zhidong, the subject of this biography. Which harms the censors meant, and what reasons the Naval Office gave, the biography does not record.
张之洞针对这几种主张上了一份议奏。他的议奏另拟一条干路，「自京外盧溝橋起，經河南以達湖北漢口鎮」，以河为界分南北两段，并非京通线。议奏中明确排出了目标次序：「修路之利，以通土貨、厚民生為最大，徵兵、轉餉次之」。目标的轻重被明明白白摆上桌面——作者认为，这个排序是这篇议奏最容易被略过、也最见功夫的地方。

Zhang Zhidong answered these proposals with a memorial. The memorial proposes a separate trunk line, running from Lugou Bridge outside the capital through Henan to Hankou in Hubei, divided by the river into northern and southern sections; it is not the Beijing-Tongzhou line. The memorial sets out an explicit ranking of goals: "In building a railway, the greatest benefit lies in moving local goods and enriching the people's livelihood; raising troops and forwarding supplies come second." The relative weight of the goals is laid plainly on the table. In the author's view, that ranking is the easiest thing to skim past in this memorial, and the place where the real craft sits.
议奏逐条列「利」，传文留下了编号：利一到利七，每条一两句，最后一条是「海上用兵，漕運無梗，利七」；议奏随即提出「有此七利，分段分年成之」。这组「利」是议奏自列的定性理由，传文未录任何测算。

The memorial works through a numbered list of benefits, and the biography preserves the numbering: benefit one through benefit seven, each a sentence or two. The last reads: "Should war come by sea, grain transport will not be obstructed - benefit seven." The memorial then proposes: "With these seven benefits, let it be completed section by section, year by year." These are qualitative reasons the memorial itself lists; the recorded text gives no quantities.
结果是「得旨報可，遂有移楚之命」。朝廷准了这份奏请，随后有调他赴湖广之命。需要说清楚的是，「得旨報可」只是准奏，不等于已经开工；张之洞本传没有记议奏所提线路的工期、用款、拆迁，其后记他奏开炼铁厂「資路用」，后文另记「三十四年，督辦粵漢鐵路」，那是粤汉铁路，并非议奏所拟自卢沟桥经河南至汉口的干路；同卷《王文韶传》记有京汉铁路兴筑，是否即此线，本文不作断定，也不替他补写这些细节。

The outcome: "The memorial received an approving rescript, and there followed the order transferring him to Huguang." The throne approved the request, and an order sending him to Huguang followed. Be clear: "approved by rescript" means the memorial was accepted, not that work began. Zhang's own biography records no schedule, outlay, or relocations for the line he proposed. It goes on to record his petition for an ironworks to supply the railway. Later it records that in the thirty-fourth year he was put in charge of the Canton-Hankou railway; that is a different line from the trunk his memorial proposed, from Lugou Bridge through Henan to Hankou. The biography of Wang Wenshao in the same chapter records the building of the Beijing-Hankou railway; whether that is this line, this article does not decide, and it will not supply the missing details.
传文对他有一句评语：「蒞官所至，必有興作。務宏大，不問費多寡」。传文同时记他任疆寄数十年，「及卒，家不增一畝」。一种解释是，这句话与前面那份编号清单出自同一种风格——敢开大摊子，也肯把摊子一条条写出来；至于花费，评语说他不问多寡，传文并未举出具体用款数字。作者认为，结合「家不增一畝」，“不问花费”不宜读作为私谋利。

The biography passes a verdict on him: "Wherever he took office, he had works begun. He aimed at the grand, and did not ask how much it cost." It also records that after decades as a provincial official, "at his death, his family had not gained a single mu of land." One reading: that verdict and the numbered list share the same style - bold enough to open big undertakings, willing to write each out item by item. As for spending, the verdict says he did not ask the amount; the biography gives no figures. In the author's view, read with the qualifier about his family's land, "did not ask how much it cost" should not be taken as spending for private gain.
其次，那段议奏文字是史书所录的文字，未必是他逐字说过的话；本文所引文字均按史书所录转述。那组「利」是他自列的定性理由，传文未录任何测算，不能当作成本收益分析来读。

Second, the memorial text is documentary text as the historians recorded it, not necessarily words he spoke verbatim; all text quoted in this article is reported as the history records it. That set of "benefits" is a list of qualitative reasons he compiled himself; the recorded text gives no quantities, and it cannot be read as cost-benefit analysis.

再次，张之洞本传没有记议奏所提线路的工期、用款、拆迁，其后记他奏开炼铁厂「資路用」，另记「三十四年，督辦粵漢鐵路」，那是粤汉铁路，与议奏所拟线路不是同一条；同卷《王文韶传》有京汉铁路兴筑的记载，是否同一线路无法确定，本文不替他补写；「得旨報可」只是准奏，不等于已经开工，更不等于办成。本文也不把原文没有的公元年份换算出来，更不会说他事先知道结果——他写下那些「利」的时候，看到的只是清单，不是成绩单。

Third, Zhang's own biography records no schedule, outlay, or relocations for the proposed line. It goes on to record his petition for an ironworks to supply the railway, and also records that in the thirty-fourth year he was put in charge of the Canton-Hankou railway, which is not the same line as the one his memorial proposed. The biography of Wang Wenshao in the same chapter records the building of the Beijing-Hankou railway, but whether it is the same line cannot be determined, and this article does not fill in the gaps. "Approved by rescript" is approval, not the start of work, still less a finished line. This article also converts no Common Era years the original does not have, and will not say he knew the outcome in advance: when he wrote those numbered benefits, what lay before him was a checklist, not a report card.
本文主要据《清史稿·张之洞传》，另引同卷《王文韶传》一条，无《清史稿》以外的记载对照；议奏文字按史书所录转述，未必是逐字原话；「利」为定性理由，传文未录测算；张之洞本传未记议奏所拟线路的工期、用款、拆迁，另记督办粤汉铁路，与议奏所拟线路不同；同卷《王文韶传》所记京汉铁路兴筑是否即此线，未作断定；「得旨報可」仅为准奏，不等于开工；不换算公元年份，亦不假定他事先知道结果。

This article rests mainly on one source, the biography of Zhang Zhidong in the Draft History of the Qing, plus one lead from the biography of Wang Wenshao in the same chapter, with no record outside the Draft History for comparison. The memorial text is reported as the historians recorded it and may not be verbatim. The "benefits" are qualitative reasons, and the recorded text gives no quantities. Zhang's own biography records no schedule, outlay, or relocations for the proposed line; it separately records his charge of the Canton-Hankou railway, a different line from the one proposed. Whether the Beijing-Hankou railway recorded in the biography of Wang Wenshao in the same chapter is this line is left undecided. "Approved by rescript" means approval only, not the start of work. No Common Era years are converted, and no foreknowledge of the outcome is assumed.

dispositions.rationale: 首句先点明张之洞的议奏写于一场“修不修、修在哪里”的多方争执。随后按修京通、请停办、试修边地以便用兵、改修德州济宁路以利漕运的顺序，逐一写出各方的主张与理由，不补造身份。最后说明传文在这些主张之后才录张之洞议奏。中英文同步。
